item.title: Zero Trust in 2026: beyond the buzzword
item.dc:creator: deniz
item.content:encoded:
Ten years after "zero trust" entered the enterprise vocabulary, most organizations still treat it as a product to purchase rather than an architecture to practice. The gap between the two is where breaches live.

In our incident-response work across 300+ enterprise environments, the pattern is consistent: flat networks behind strong perimeters. The badge reader is state-of-the-art; the east-west traffic is wide open.

Identity is the new perimeter — really

Every access decision should be scored against device posture, session risk and behavioral baseline. Not once at login — continuously. Teams that adopted continuous verification cut lateral-movement dwell time by 84% in our 2025 dataset.

"The question is never whether an attacker gets a credential. It's what that credential is worth once they have it."

Where to start in 2026

Segment your crown-jewel systems first, instrument everything second, and only then negotiate with vendors. Architecture before procurement — always.
item.excerpt:encoded: What a decade of zero-trust rollouts taught us about identity, segmentation and the myths vendors still sell.

item.title: Hardening Kubernetes clusters: a field guide
item.dc:creator: deniz
item.content:encoded:
Kubernetes ships permissive by default. This field guide walks through the controls we deploy first on every engagement: admission policies, network segmentation, workload identity and runtime detection.

Start with the control plane

Audit logging, API-server flags and etcd encryption come before anything workload-level. If the control plane is soft, nothing above it matters.

From there: enforce Pod Security standards, default-deny network policies, and rotate service-account tokens aggressively.
item.excerpt:encoded: The controls we deploy first on every Kubernetes engagement — from admission policies to runtime detection.

item.title: Why hardware firewalls still matter
item.dc:creator: deniz
item.content:encoded:
Cloud-delivered security is everywhere, yet the perimeter appliance refuses to die — for good reason. Line-rate inspection, deterministic latency and physical isolation are still hard to replicate in software alone.

Where appliances win

Industrial networks, trading floors and regulated on-prem estates all share one requirement: predictable performance under attack. Dedicated silicon delivers it.
item.excerpt:encoded: Line-rate inspection, deterministic latency and physical isolation — why the perimeter appliance refuses to die.

item.title: Post-quantum cryptography: what to do now
item.dc:creator: deniz
item.content:encoded:
"Harvest now, decrypt later" is not a hypothetical. Inventory your cryptography today: where keys live, which protocols carry long-lived secrets, and what breaks when algorithms change.

A pragmatic migration path

Hybrid key exchange first, certificate agility second, hardware roots of trust third. None of it requires waiting for final standards to be universal.
item.excerpt:encoded: Inventory your cryptography today — a pragmatic path toward post-quantum readiness.
